Indian Standard
METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF FAT IN CHEESE BY VAN GULIK METHOD
0.
0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 9 March 1979, after the draft finalized by the Dairy Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Van Gulik method is used for rapid and routine determination of fat in cheese. The use of standardized and calibrated apparatus and the adoption of uniform method for determination of fat in cheese by this method will enable one to obtain comparable results, within a reasonable degree of accuracy. To achieve this end, it is expected that this standard would help in providing a uniform procedure for determination of fat in chrese by the Van Gulik method, and IS : 9105-1979* would be helpful in standardization and calibration of the apparatus. It should be emphasized that the method prescribed in this standard for routine purposts only, and while this gives results comparable with gravimetric method, this cannot be substituted for gravimetric method, which will have to be used for reference purposes.
is designed

0.3

0.4 In the formation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from IS0 3433-1975 ` Cheese - Determination of fat content Van Gblik method ' issued by the International Organization for StandaGdization. 0.5 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : Z-19601_.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the procedure in cheese by the Van Gulik method.

However, it may not give completely satisfactory results when it is applied to cheeses with an internal mould ( blue-veined cheeses ). 2. PRINCIPLE 2.1 Dissolution of the protein with sulphuric acid, followed by separation of the fat of the cheese in a Van Gulik butyrometer by centrifuging, the separation being assisted by the addition of a small quantity of amyl alcohol, and direct reading of the fat content on the butyrometer scale. 3. Is:9070~1979 5. PROCEDURE 5.1 Preparation of the Test Sample

5.1.1 Prior to analysis, remove the rind or smear or mouldy surface layer of the cheese, to provide a sample which is representative of the cheese as usually consumed. Grind the sample by means of an appropriate device ( 3.9 )_ Mix the g round mass quickly, and if possible grind a second time and again mix thoroughly. If the sample is difficult to be ground, mix it thoroughly by intensive stirring and kneading. 5.1.2 Transfer the test sample to an air-tight container to await analysis, which should be carried out on the same day. If delay is unavoidable, take all precaution to ensure proper preservation of the sample and to prevent condensation of moisture on the inside surface of Clean the device after grinding each sampJe. the container. to the nearest 0.005 g, 3 g of the test 5.2 Test Portion - Weigh, sample ( 5.1 ) into the weighing device ( 3.8 ) fitted to a suitable stopper, or into a capsule, or on plastic sheet. 5.3 Determination

5.3.1 If a stopper with a weighing device is used, close the neck of the butyromerer ( 3.1 ) with this stopper, in&din g weighing device and test portion, and add sulphuric acid ( 4.1 ) to the small opening until the acid level reaches a height of about two-thirds of the body of the butyrometer and the weighing device is compietely surrounded with sulphnric acid. If no weighing device in the large stopper is used, close rhe small opening of the butyrometer with the small stopper and let sulphuric acid run into the butyrometer through the neck until the acid level Transfer reaches a height of about half the body of the butyrometer. If plastic sheet is used, transfer the the cheese to the butyrometer. Close the neck with the large stopper, invert the cheese with the sheet. butyrometer x+rd remove the small stopper. 5.3.2 Place the butyrometer with its neck ( that is, large opening downwards for 5.minutes in the water-bath ( 3.6 ) at 65 &- 2�C. 5.3.3 Remove the butyrometer thoroughly for 10 seconds. 5.3.4 Repeat the operations ,protein is completely dissolved. dissolution of protein. Repeat protein has been dissolved. from the water-bath and shake ) it

specified in 5.3.2 and 5.3.3 until the One hour is usually needed for complete the procedure for 15 minutes after the

NOTE -- Mechanical shaking devices may be used provided that their use produces the same results as the manual procedure specified above.

IS : 9070 - 1979 5.3.5 Remove the butyrometer from the water-bath and add, after thorough shaking of the butyrometer, 1 ml of amyl alcohol ( 4.2 ) to the small opening. Immediately shake the butyrometer for at least 3 seconds.
5.3.6 Add sulphuric acid to the small opening until the level reaches Close immediately with the small the 35 percent graduation mark. stopper and invert the butyrometer. 5.3.7 As soon as the fat has ascended into the body, shake the butyroInvert again so that the acid drains meter thoroughly for 10 seconds. out of the stem. Repeat shaking and inverting twice. 5.3.8 Place the butyrometer neck downwards for 5 minutes in the water-bath, the water level should b-e above the top of the fat column in the butyrometer. 5.3.9 Remove the butyrometer from the water-bath, adjust the large stopper to bring the fat column on the scale and centrifuge the butyrometer for 10 minutes at a relative centrifugal acceleration of 350 + 50 g. 5.3.10 Place the butyrometer neck downwards to the water-bath for 5 minutes. Maintain the water level above the top of the fat column in the butyrometer. 5.3.II Remove the butyrometer from the water-bath and carefully adjust the large stopper to bring the bottom of the fat column, with the minimum movement of the column, to a graduation mark, preferably a main graduation mark. This should preferably be done by slightly withdrawing the stopper and not by forcing it further into the neck. Note the scale reading coincident with the bottom of the fat column and then, taking care that the fat column does not move, as quickly as possible note the scale reading coincident with the lowest point of the-fat meniscus This reading shall be taken to the nearest at the top of the fat column. half of the smallest scale division (025 percent). While readings are being taken, the butyrometer shall be held vertically and the eye shall be level tyith the point of reading.
NOTE - If the fat is turbid or dark in colour or if there is white or black material at the bottom of the fat column, the value for the fat content may not be accurate.
